utility.notes: Chugach Electric Association is a member-owned electric cooperative. Its own net metering materials confirm it serves the 'Anchorage Bowl' (the area within the Municipality of Anchorage's Building Safety Service Area) as the interconnecting utility for net-metered systems.

value.name: Chugach Electric Association, Inc.
value.notes: Chugach is a member-owned rural electric cooperative rather than a shareholder-owned investor utility, but it functions as the sole interconnecting distribution/generation utility for net-metered systems in its service territory.

county.notes: Alaska has no counties; boroughs are the county-equivalent. The Municipality of Anchorage is a unified home-rule borough-city government (a consolidated city-borough), with a single Development Services Department administering permitting for the Anchorage Building Safety Service Area (BSSA) — essentially the Anchorage Bowl. Areas outside the BSSA (Eklutna, Chugiak, Eagle River, Bird, Girdwood, and parts of the hillside) follow a simpler land-use-only permit path within the same municipal government, per the City's own solar PV handout.

permit_authority.value: Municipality of Anchorage Development Services Department, Building Safety Division
permit_authority.notes: A single consolidated municipal government administers permitting for the entire Municipality of Anchorage. The Development Services Department publishes a dedicated, dated, signed solar-specific handout (AG.28, Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Permit Process/Checklist) distinguishing the permit path for locations inside vs. outside the Anchorage Building Safety Service Area (BSSA).

interconnection_url.notes: Chugach's own net metering page confirms the application process and a $270 non-refundable application fee, and states that member-installed renewable generation offsets monthly usage and that excess generation can be sold back to the utility, but directs readers to the utility's separate Operating Tariff (Electric), Section 89.3, for the exact net metering and buyback credit rate structure — that tariff document was not independently fetched this session, so the exact per-kWh credit/buyback rate is left unconfirmed rather than guessed.

battery_programs.notes: Chugach's own Application for Net Metering Installation form asks applicants to describe any 'ancillary power equipment (battery storage, transfer switches, etc.)' as part of the system's technical description, but this is an interconnection/technical disclosure requirement, not a confirmed financial battery incentive program. No such program was independently confirmed this session.

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own dedicated solar PV handout (AG.28). A detached single-family home or duplex inside the BSSA requires both structural and electrical permits (no separate electrical plan review, but an electrical inspection is required); the same property type outside the BSSA instead needs only a land-use permit with a land-use (zoning) plan review — no electrical or structural plan review or inspections.

value: Electrical inspection — inspector reviews the PV spec sheets and installation instructions on site, plus the copy of utility (Chugach) approval
Structural inspection — inspector reviews the approved structural plans in the field
Both electrical and structural inspections must be approved before a certificate of completion is issued, which is required to close the permit
Ground-mount installations additionally require an as-built survey submitted to Land Use plan review before a certificate of completion can be obtained
inspection_steps.notes: Inspections can be requested online, by phone (343-8300, 24/7), or by fax. Applies to the inside-BSSA structural+electrical permit path; the outside-BSSA land-use-only path does not require electrical or structural inspections.

value.notes: Per the City's own handout: Development Services makes best efforts to review one- and two-family PV permit applications within 4 business days (10 business days for other PV application types, e.g. 3-4 unit or commercial buildings) — explicitly described as typical, not guaranteed. This is the plan-review turnaround only, not total project/construction time. Permit applications expire by limitation if no permit is issued within 360 days, or if authorized work is suspended/abandoned for 360 days after starting.

value.program_or_pathway: Structural + electrical permit path for a detached single-family home or duplex located within the Anchorage Building Safety Service Area (BSSA); a simpler land-use-only permit path applies instead outside the BSSA.
other_conditions: The BSSA is essentially the Anchorage Bowl; Eklutna, Chugiak, Eagle River, Bird, Girdwood, and some hillside areas are outside the BSSA and follow the land-use-only path (no electrical/structural plan review or inspections).
Chugach Electric's net metering program caps nameplate generating capacity at 25kW, per Chugach's own Application for Net Metering Installation form.
Utility (Chugach) approval of the interconnection is a prerequisite step the City's own handout instructs applicants to complete first, before/alongside the City permit process.
